title: The man of God from Judah against the altar of Bethel: "Josiah by name" (1 Kgs 13:1–3)
speaker: An unnamed man of God from Judah (Jadon in Josephus)
description: At Jeroboam's altar in Bethel a man of God announces that a son named Josiah will be born to David's house and will sacrifice the priests of the high places on it and burn human bones on it (1 Kgs 13:2).
in_text_interpretation: 2 Kgs 23:15–18 narrates Josiah burning bones on the Bethel altar "according to the LORD's word which the man of God proclaimed" and sparing that prophet's tomb. The text itself states the fulfilment.

interpretations.label: Predictive prophecy in Jeroboam's time, fulfilled by Josiah at Bethel (c. 622/621)
proponents: Josephus (Ant. 10.4.4: the prophet "Jadon"; fulfilled "after three hundred and sixty-one years")
D. Guzik (citing Knapp: "more than three hundred years")
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: 2 Kgs 23:16–18 explicitly cites the earlier word and the prophet's tomb. Historical evidence: none external for either the prophecy or the desecration of the Bethel altar was read in this session. Objection: critical scholarship dates the 1 Kings 13 narrative later (next interpretation).

interpretations.label: A later narrative shaped in the light of Josiah's reform (not an early prediction)
proponents: S. R. Driver (1891): "a narrative not probably of very early origin"
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: Driver notes that the narrative dates from a time when the names of both the Judean prophet and the old prophet were no longer remembered (p. 183); he does not argue this point at length in the pages read. Objection: the traditional reading treats the naming of Josiah as genuine prediction; neither position is testable from external evidence.
